hook: Air Force MISREP #8799515 documents an ISR crew's observation of four UAP over approximately 27 seconds during an Arabian Gulf mission in 2020, with sequential appearance times logged to the second and visual tracking disrupted by cloud coverage.
why_it_matters: This report demonstrates that U.S. Air Forces Central (AFCENT) is actively using the standardized MISREP format to formally document UAP encounters during operational ISR missions, confirming institutional integration of UAP reporting into combat command workflows. The second-level timing detail (17:36:22, 17:36:30, 17:36:49) suggests the crew was recording against sensor timestamps rather than estimating, lending precision to the observation record. The explicit 'NO' answer to the Advanced Capabilities field, combined with heavy operational redaction, reflects the structured but intelligence-constrained nature of AARO-format submissions.

key_findings.finding: Four UAP appeared sequentially over approximately 27 seconds, with two observed side by side at the same timestamp — consistent with the 'line of dots followed by a trailing dot' characterization in the war.gov manifest.

quotes.text: AT APPROX 1736Z 4 UAP WERE OBSERVED BENEATH (b)(1)1.4a 1X UAP OBSERVED AT 17:36:22, 2X UAP OBSERVED SIDE BY SIDE AT 17:36:30, AND 1X UAP OBSERVED AT 17:36:49.

key_findings.finding: Cloud coverage actively disrupted sensor tracking and prevented a clear visual on the UAP, limiting what the ISR platform could capture.

quotes.text: CLOUD COVERAGE OBSTRUCTED (b)(1)1.4a FROM FOLLOWING AND GETTING A CLEAR VISUAL. (SEE ISR 1).

key_findings.finding: The reporting crew's assessment explicitly answered 'NO' to whether UAP exhibited advanced capabilities or anomalous materials, a required structured field in the MISREP UAP section.

quotes.text: UAP Advanced Capabilities And/Or Materials  (yes/no; if yes, describe): NO

key_findings.finding: The mission falls under Air Forces Central (AFCENT) and was conducted by a U.S. Air Force unit; all personnel identifiers, the specific operation, aircraft callsign, and ISR sensor details are withheld under national security exemptions (b)(1)1.4a).

key_findings.finding: The report is classified SECRET and will not be declassified until June 3, 2048 — a 28-year hold from the present day — indicating the operational context remains sensitive beyond the UAP observation itself.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This MISREP was submitted to AARO using the standardized UAP reporting format with structured fields (UAP Event Type, Maneuverability, Signatures, Advanced Capabilities) that AARO requires from military operators.
The classification caveat 'REL TO USA, FVEY' appears in the takeoff gentext, indicating the report or portions of it are releasable to Five Eyes partners.
